facts.content: Irritant/contact dermatitis of hands with a temporal relation to cleaning chemicals and glove nonuse.
facts.source_text: Irritant/contact dermatitis of hands (palmar) — temporal relation to cleaning chemicals, glove nonuse

facts.content: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus may impair skin barrier healing.

facts.content: Avoid triggers and maintain strict glove use with cleaning.
facts.source_text: Avoid triggers; strict glove use with cleaning

facts.content: Prescribe medium-potency topical corticosteroid for hands to be applied twice daily for 10 to 14 days, then taper.

facts.content: Recommend gentle skin care using fragrance-free cleansers, avoiding hot water, and frequent moisturization.
facts.source_text: Gentle skin care: fragrance-free cleansers; avoid hot water; frequent moisturization

facts.content: Advise return or emergency precautions if symptoms worsen, spread, or show no improvement in 10 to 14 days.
facts.source_text: Return/ED precautions: worsening, spreading, increased pain/bleeding, no improvement in 10–14 days

facts.content: Work may require modified duties or brief time off until pain and fissures improve.

facts.content: Continue Metformin and optimize glycemic control to aid healing.

facts.content: Reassess patient in 1 to 2 weeks and consider alternative diagnosis or treatment if no improvement.
